findings.issue_text: Review scaffold: `docs/metareview/reviews/mrv-20260824-172830826786000-task-done-task-001-377c2c6a.md` — verdict **NEEDS_REVISION**.
packages/core/CalendarManager.ts:230 — TODO left in task-done diff: `// TODO: i18n this string?` on "Notes have been hidden by the organizer"
PASS — no blocking findings
PASS — no blocking findings
PASS — no blocking findings

packages/core/EventManager.ts:118-119 — `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` then `.integration` with no optional chaining. Empty/null destinationCalendar (produced by handleNewBooking.ts:1063 and every trpc/webhook caller) + Google Meet location now throws TypeError instead of falling back to Cal Video. Every other converted site in the diff uses `?.` here.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:254-256 and :315-317 — tautological fallback: `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find(cal => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. The find only runs when externalCalendarId is falsy, so it compares against undefined and never matches. updateEvent passes `calendarId: undefined`; deleteEvent silently falls back to "primary" and swallows the resulting 404. Old fallback `destinationCalendar.externalId` is effectively deleted.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:1077-1078 — `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` is a silent no-op when destinationCalendar is null (organizer + event type both lack one). The co-hosts' calendars are dropped — exactly the case the task exists to fix.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:479, 511-542 — `let credential` (implicit `any`) is declared outside the new per-reference loop. If a later reference's credential misses both the in-memory list and the DB lookup, it silently retains the previous host's credential (or is undefined on iteration 1) and is passed unguarded to `updateEvent`, which dereferences it. No `if (credential)` guard, unlike createAllCalendarEvents.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:206-209 (updateLocation) — reads `result.externalId` / `result.credentialId`, but CalendarManager.updateEvent (CalendarManager.ts:312-322) never populates either (only createEvent was updated). Both are now always undefined, where the old code fell back to evt.destinationCalendar. Every location edit writes a booking reference with no externalCalendarId/credentialId.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:169-170 — `credentialId: isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined`. The non-calendar (video) branch previously carried `result.credentialId`; video booking references now always get undefined, breaking later credential-scoped video update/delete. Only the calendar half of the ternary was migrated.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:376-382 — the no-credentialId branch calls `createEvent(c, event)` without the third `externalId` arg, so result.externalId is undefined and the reference at :169 gets `externalCalendarId: undefined`. Previously sourced from evt.destinationCalendar.externalId.

packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:73, packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:128, packages/lib/CalendarService.ts:156 — only Google's createEvent honors the new `credentialId` param; Lark/Office365/CalDAV still resolve `destinationCalendar[0]`. A COLLECTIVE event with N hosts on those providers creates N events all in the first host's calendar, with references recording externalCalendarIds that were never used — so update/delete later target empty calendars.

packages/core/CalendarManager.ts:267 — the returned `externalId` is the *requested* destination, not what the provider used. If one credential owns two destination calendars, both iterations write the same calendar (duplicate events) and both references store a wrong externalCalendarId. The `Calendar.createEvent(event, credentialId)` contract (Calendar.d.ts:221) promises per-credential resolution almost no implementation provides.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:553-565 — the reschedule/seat-merge path still uses `booking.references.find(...)` and deletes only the first old calendar event; N−1 stale events are orphaned on other hosts' calendars.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:2146-2176 — Google Meet handling still assumes one google_calendar reference (`findIndex`, `results[googleCalIndex]`). With multiple Google destinations each createEvent requests its own conference; only the first Meet link reaches the booking/attendees.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:1874-1878 — `connect: { id: evt.destinationCalendar[0].id }`; Booking.destinationCalendar is still a single FK, so N−1 collective destinations are never persisted. Cancel/confirm/webhook paths rebuild a 1-element array from that column, so multi-host info exists only inside handleNewBooking and BookingReference rows.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:1063-1078 — no dedup by (credentialId, externalId). Two hosts sharing a destination calendar, or a host matching eventType.destinationCalendar, yields duplicate events and duplicate references in the same external calendar.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:334-385 — for a destination with no credentialId it still fans out to every credential of that integration type, and this now runs per destination: N destinations × M credentials = duplicate events.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:1063-1078 — round-robin and dynamic group bookings still get only the organizer's calendar, and the TODO that documented this gap was deleted, leaving it undocumented.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:423-476 — the recurring-cancellation block (and the legacy `else` at :474) is now nested inside the new per-reference loop. Each already iterates all user credentials × all remaining bookings, so N calendar references produce N× duplicate deleteEvent calls.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:448-459 — inside that block, `updBooking.references.find(...)` still picks one calendar reference per booking and only iterates `bookingToDelete.user.credentials` (no DB fallback like the non-recurring branch), so co-hosts' recurring events are never deleted.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:341-360, :517-540 and packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:433-441 — new `prisma.credential.findUnique({ where: { id: credentialId } })` fallbacks load ANY credential row by primary key with no userId/teamId/host scoping. Previously the trust boundary was this.calendarCredentials / bookingToDelete.user.credentials. Any path that can influence a DestinationCalendar.credentialId or BookingReference.credentialId becomes a cross-tenant calendar write/delete with another tenant's OAuth token, carrying full attendee PII. handleCancelBooking is reachable by an attendee holding a booking uid. The legitimate host set is known here, so scoping is cheap.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:147-154 — createEvent now resolves via `destinationCalendar.find(cal => cal.credentialId === credentialId)` falling back to "primary". DestinationCalendar.credentialId is nullable (EventManager explicitly handles that branch), so for legacy rows the find misses and attendee names/emails/notes are written to the user's primary calendar instead of the deliberately segregated destination calendar. Silent confidentiality regression.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:315-322 — the dead-fallback delete targets "primary", the 404 is swallowed (`if (err.code === 404) return resolve()`), so cancellation is recorded as successful while the event with attendee PII remains on the real destination calendar indefinitely, masked from operators.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/organizations/create.handler.ts:151-153 — inverted and unrelated: `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` → `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`, both ternaries now the same polarity. With billing enabled the org gets a live `slug` AND `requestedSlug` before payment while `isOrganizationVerified: false` — arbitrary org subdomains can be squatted for free and served under <slug>.cal.com. With billing disabled the org gets no slug at all.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:590-596 — `console.error(message)` deleted from the updateAllCalendarEvents catch; `message` is still computed and discarded, so calendar update failures are now completely silent. The catch also returns `[]` when the throw preceded `calendarReference` assignment, so callers inspecting results for failures see none (previously always a `{ success: false }` result).
packages/core/EventManager.ts:531-542 — one unresolvable credential throws out of the loop and aborts updates for all other hosts; no per-reference failure isolation.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:723-762 — loadUsers fully rewritten (ternary → try/catch). Empty/undefined dynamicUserList now yields HttpError 500 "Unable to load users" instead of an empty list handled downstream; inner HttpErrors including 404s are re-mapped to 400. Unrelated to the fix.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:731-741 — the dynamic-user select silently dropped `organization: { select: { slug: true } }` (and the "Don't leak to client" comment) while IsFixedAwareUser (:355) still declares `organization: { slug: string }` and getBookerUrl consumes it. Not caught at compile time due to the `as IsFixedAwareUser[]` cast at :870 — the type now lies.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:688-689, 992, 1077 — SchedulingType enum comparisons replaced with magic strings `["COLLECTIVE","ROUND_ROBIN"].includes(...)` / `=== "COLLECTIVE"`, losing compile-time checking on a discriminator that has a named enum.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:993-996 — team members now carry `firstName: ""` / `lastName: ""`, fields absent from the TeamMember/Person types (Calendar.d.ts:28-46); dead values that flow into emails and webhooks.
packages/types/Calendar.d.ts:182 — new `schedulingType` field on CalendarEvent, set at handleNewBooking.ts:1071, read by nothing anywhere; dead payload that also leaks into webhook payloads.
packages/core/builders/CalendarEvent/builder.ts:1-2 — `import { Prisma, Booking }` split into type/value imports; pure lint-style drive-by.
packages/core/CalendarManager.ts:230 — user-visible copy change "organiser" → "organizer", unrelated (and still TODO-flagged for i18n).
packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:370, 383 — typo rename orginalBookingDuration → originalBookingDuration; harmless but unrelated.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:987-1005 — `users.length > 1 ? ... : []` guard replaced by unconditional `users.slice(1).map(...)`; equivalent today but beyond what the fix required.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:1063 returns `null` for "no destination calendars" while every other producer (handleCancelBooking.ts:251, confirm.handler.ts:175, webhook.ts:119, paypal-webhook.ts:152, bookingReminder.ts:130, requestReschedule.handler.ts:240) returns `[]`. Two representations of one state on a public webhook payload — apps/web/playwright/webhook.e2e.ts:119,373 still assert `null` while :249 was changed to `[]`.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:344-358, :517-531, handleCancelBooking.ts:433-440 — the same "not in calendarCredentials → prisma.credential.findUnique → hand-map" block is copy-pasted three times (twice with the app.slug include, once without). Credential resolution leaking out of EventManager/CalendarManager into the cancel handler; belongs behind one getCredentialById() helper.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:987-999 — teamDestinationCalendars collected as a side effect inside the teamMemberPromises .map(), coupling "who are the attendees" to "which calendars do we write to"; the COLLECTIVE fan-out rule now lives in the booking handler while EventManager, which owns fan-out, knows nothing about it.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:339-372 and :509-551 — N+1: `await prisma.credential.findUnique` plus serialized `await createEvent`/`updateEvent` per destination/reference (the sibling branch at :380 still uses Promise.all), plus a repeated linear `this.calendarCredentials.filter(...)[0]` per reference — O(refs × credentials) where a Map<id, credential> built once is O(1).

packages/core/EventManager.ts:63 — EventManagerUser.destinationCalendar is still `DestinationCalendar | null` while CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar is now an array: same concept, two shapes, same file.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:418 and packages/core/EventManager.ts:479 — `bookingCalendarReference` / `calendarReference` are now arrays but keep singular names, reading as single values at every use site.

No tests added or changed for the new behavior. Zero test coverage of destinationCalendar exists in the repo and no unit test covers the multi-destination createAllCalendarEvents/updateAllCalendarEvents loops; the only test touched is a Playwright snapshot value.

Bottom line:** the diff does not deliver its stated intent (the null-`destinationCalendar` collective case silently drops co-host calendars, and non-Google providers ignore the per-credential parameter entirely), introduces at least one guaranteed crash and several silent data-loss paths, carries an unrelated inverted condition in org creation with a real security consequence, and widens credential lookup past its previous ownership boundary. Concur with **NEEDS_REVISION**.

goldens.comment: A null reference occurs in GoogleCalendarService.createEvent() and updateEvent() when mainHostDestinationCalendar is destructured from evt.destinationCalendar but evt.destinationCalendar is null or an empty array, causing mainHostDestinationCalendar to be undefined.
The optional chaining on mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration is redundant since you already check mainHostDestinationCalendar in the ternary condition.

Logic error: when externalCalendarId is provided, you're searching for a calendar where externalId === externalCalendarId, but this will always fail since you're looking for a calendar that matches itself. Should likely find by credentialId or use different logic.

Logic inversion in organization creation: The slug property is now conditionally set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, instead of when it's false as originally intended. This change, combined with requestedSlug still being set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, results in both properties being set when billing is enabled, and neither when disabled

The Calendar interface now requires createEvent(event, credentialId), but some implementations (e.g., Lark/Office365) still declare createEvent(event) only—this breaks the interface contract (also applies to other locations in the PR).

The `credential` may be undefined when passed to `updateEvent` if `reference.credentialId` is set but the credential is not found. This can lead to a runtime error when `updateEvent` is called with an undefined credential, which should be handled to prevent crashes.

adjudication.rationale:
In `GoogleCalendarService.updateEvent` and `deleteEvent`, the new fallback is:
`externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find(cal => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`.
Because the `.find(...)` branch only executes when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, the comparison inside becomes `cal.externalId === undefined`, which will not match any normal calendar entry. This means when `externalCalendarId` is not provided, the code no longer falls back to any `destinationCalendar` externalId (the old `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` behavior is effectively removed), and the computed calendar id will be `undefined` in that case (leaving only whatever later defaulting logic exists). The tautological/ineffective fallback described by the finding is directly verifiable in the diff.

The candidate explicitly notes that only Google honors the new `credentialId` parameter and that Lark/Office365/CalDAV still behave as before (using `destinationCalendar[0]`), which is the same underlying problem: other implementations not updated to the new API/parameter usage, causing incorrect behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/core/CalendarManager.ts:267 — the returned `externalId` is the *requested* destination, not what the provider used. If one credential owns two destination calendars, both iterations write the same calendar (duplicate events) and both references store a wrong externalCalendarId. The `Calendar.createEvent(event, credentialId)` contract (Calendar.d.ts:221) promises per-credential resolution almost no implementation provides.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents`, the loop calls `createEvent(credential, event, destination.externalId)` for each destination, but `CalendarManager.createEvent` does not pass that `externalId` into the provider; it always calls `calendar.createEvent(calEvent, credential.id)`. In `GoogleCalendarService.createEvent`, the chosen calendar is `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find(cal => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId`, i.e., selection is only by `credentialId` and not by the per-iteration requested `destination.externalId`. Therefore, if `event.destinationCalendar` contains multiple entries with the same `credentialId` but different `externalId`, each iteration will resolve to the same (first) matching calendar and insert duplicate events into that one calendar, while `CalendarManager` returns/stores `externalId` from the requested destination, which can be wrong relative to what was actually used.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/core/EventManager.ts:334-385 — for a destination with no credentialId it still fans out to every credential of that integration type, and this now runs per destination: N destinations × M credentials = duplicate events.

adjudication.rationale: In `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` (around 334+), the new array-based logic loops `for (const destination of event.destinationCalendar)`. When a `destination` has no `credentialId`, it executes an else-branch that filters `this.calendarCredentials` by `c.type === destination.integration` and then creates events for *all* matching credentials. Because this else-branch is inside the per-destination loop, multiple destinations without `credentialId` (especially if they share the same `integration`) will re-run the same fan-out each time, producing N destinations × M credentials event creations (duplicates relative to the intended “one per destination”). This behavior is directly visible in the diff and is not guarded against.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/core/EventManager.ts:341-360, :517-540 and packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:433-441 — new `prisma.credential.findUnique({ where: { id: credentialId } })` fallbacks load ANY credential row by primary key with no userId/teamId/host scoping. Previously the trust boundary was this.calendarCredentials / bookingToDelete.user.credentials. Any path that can influence a DestinationCalendar.credentialId or BookingReference.credentialId becomes a cross-tenant calendar write/delete with another tenant's OAuth token, carrying full attendee PII. handleCancelBooking is reachable by an attendee holding a booking uid. The legitimate host set is known here, so scoping is cheap.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces multiple fallbacks that fetch a credential by primary key only (no userId/teamId scoping) and then uses it to perform calendar operations. In `packages/core/EventManager.ts` the new code path in `createAllCalendarEvents` (around the added prisma.credential.findUnique for `destination.credentialId`) and in the updated booking update logic (new loop over calendar references with a similar findUnique for `reference.credentialId`) will accept any credential row matching that ID and then call `createEvent`/`updateEvent` with it. In `packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts` a similar fallback was added when `bookingToDelete.user.credentials` doesn’t contain the referenced credential: it does `prisma.credential.findUnique({ where: { id: credentialId } })` and then uses it with `getCalendar(...).deleteEvent(...)`. These lookups are unscoped and therefore remove the prior implicit boundary of only using credentials already associated with the host/user in memory; if a `credentialId` in `DestinationCalendar` or a booking reference can be influenced/corrupted, the code will act using another tenant’s OAuth credential. That specific lack of scoping is directly verifiable in the diff.
